mainTopic: רבא and רבי יהודה on מוקצה; the משנה and גמרא on clearing bones, crumbs, pods and date pits from the table on שבת
overview: This amud first finishes a discussion about whether רבא holds like רבי יהודה, who is strict about מוקצה and נולד. The גמרא explains that innards given to a cat were planned for the cat before שבת, so they were never מוקצה. It then proves that רבא follows רבי יהודה from his ruling that a poker that breaks on יום טוב may not be burned. A new משנה follows about clearing the table on שבת: bones and shells, crumbs, pea and lentil pods, and wiping with a sponge. The גמרא reports רב נחמן's tradition that reverses בית שמאי and בית הלל, so that בית הלל are lenient like רבי שמעון. It notes that the crumbs ruling supports רבי יוחנן, and that the pods ruling follows רבי שמעון. It then shows that the sponge ruling fits רבי שמעון too, because squeezing the sponge is a פסיק רישיה. Finally, it rules on date pits and lists how different אמוראים got rid of מוקצה pits, and the פרק ends with the הדרן.

steps.title: The innards were already intended for the cat before שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers a challenge from an earlier ruling of רבא. Innards spoil quickly, so the owner already planned before שבת to give them to the cat. That means they were never set aside as מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, since it will rot, his mind was on it from yesterday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a question raised on the previous amud. The question used an earlier lenient ruling of רבא about giving animal innards to a cat to suggest that רבא does not follow רבי יהודה's strict view of מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that רבא seemed to allow something that should count as מוקצה according to רבי יהודה. The answer is that innards go bad fast, so a person decides ahead of time, from ערב שבת, that they will go to the cat. Because the person never put them out of his mind, even רבי יהודה would not call them מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind is on it (he intends to use it)
From yesterday (from before שבת or יום טוב)

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say רבא disagrees with רבי יהודה. It says the innards were never set aside in the first place, so the rules of מוקצה never came into play.

phrases.english: There, since it will rot,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the innards in רבא's earlier ruling.

phrases.english: his mind is on it from yesterday.
phrases.notes: He planned before שבת to give them to the cat.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם כֵּיוָן דְּמַסְרַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge, raised on the previous amud, against the claim that רבא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the item had been mentally set aside for use from before שבת, so it was never מוקצה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבא's lenient ruling about the innards showed that he does not accept רבי יהודה's strict rules of מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: In that case the innards were never מוקצה, because the owner always intended them for the cat. So the ruling fits even with רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Proof from רבא's teaching about a broken poker
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings support that רבא really does hold like רבי יהודה. רבא taught that a woman may not take a poker from the woodshed on יום טוב. He also taught that a poker that broke may not be used as fuel, because broken pieces of a utensil may not be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too it makes sense that רבא holds like רבי יהודה, because רבא taught: A woman may not go into the woodshed to take a poker from there. And a poker that broke may not be burned on יום טוב, because one may burn whole utensils but may not burn broken pieces of utensils.
steps.whatsHappening: After defending its claim, the גמרא now actively supports it. It quotes a public teaching of רבא that is strict about מוקצה and נולד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wood in a storehouse is stored away and not meant for use on יום טוב, so even a stick taken out as a poker is forbidden. A poker that breaks on יום טוב turns from a utensil into a 'new' thing, broken pieces that did not exist at the start of the day. Forbidding this new thing is exactly רבי יהודה's view of נולד.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is reasonable (introduces supporting evidence)
A poker (a stick for stirring a fire)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical rule for יום טוב: a whole utensil may be used as fuel, but a utensil that breaks during the day becomes a new, forbidden item (נולד) and may not be burned.

phrases.english: So too, it is reasonable
phrases.notes: This phrase brings a proof to back up what was just said.

phrases.english: that Rava holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה is strict about מוקצה and נולד.

phrases.english: as Rava taught publicly:
A woman may not enter the woodshed
phrases.notes: The stored wood there is set aside and not meant for use on the Festival.

phrases.english: to take a poker from it.
phrases.notes: Even taking a single stick to stir the fire is forbidden.

phrases.english: And a poker that broke,
phrases.notes: It broke on the Festival itself.

phrases.english: it is forbidden to burn it on a Festival,
because one may kindle with utensils
phrases.notes: A whole utensil may be moved, so it may be burned.

phrases.english: but one may not kindle with broken pieces of utensils.
phrases.notes: The broken pieces are נולד, a 'new thing' that came into being on יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא דְּרָבָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the claim in step 1, the גמרא now brings active proof for it.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבא follows רבי יהודה on מוקצה and נולד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's public teaching forbidding a poker from the woodshed, and forbidding a poker that broke on יום טוב to be burned.

steps.title: Conclusion: רבא follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof: רבא holds like רבי יהודה regarding מוקצה and נולד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion by accepting the proof from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidding the broken poker only makes sense if you hold like רבי יהודה, who forbids נולד. So the גמרא concludes that רבא follows רבי יהודה. The earlier case of the innards was not a contradiction, as step 1 showed.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it / conclude from this

steps.whatToRemember: רבא holds like רבי יהודה: מוקצה and נולד are forbidden. Food that a person planned to use before שבת (like innards for the cat) is not מוקצה, but a utensil that breaks on יום טוב becomes forbidden נולד.

phrases.english: Conclude from it.
phrases.notes: רבא holds like רבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof from step 2 and closes the topic.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא follows רבי יהודה's strict view of מוקצה and נולד.

steps.title: משנה: How to clear bones and shells off the table
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. בית שמאי allow removing bones and shells from the table directly. בית הלל say you lift the whole tabletop and shake the leftovers off.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: בית שמאי say: One may clear bones and shells off the table. And בית הלל say: One removes the whole tabletop and shakes it off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new משנה. It presents a disagreement between בית שמאי and בית הלל about cleaning up leftovers after a שבת meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי allow picking up the bones and shells themselves and taking them off the table. בית הלל treat these leftovers as things that may not be handled directly, so you move the tabletop, which is a utensil, and shake the leftovers off. The leftovers move only indirectly.

keyTerms.meaning: Bones and shells (leftovers from the meal)

steps.confusionAlert: בית הלל are not saying the table must stay dirty. They allow cleaning it, but only by moving the board and shaking it, not by handling the leftovers directly.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Beit Shammai say:
One may clear from the table
phrases.notes: Directly, by hand.

phrases.english: bones and shells.
And Beit Hillel say:
One removes the entire tabletop board
phrases.notes: The board is a utensil, so it may be moved.

phrases.english: and shakes it off.
phrases.notes: The leftovers fall off without being handled directly.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: מַעֲבִירִין מֵעַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן עֲצָמוֹת וּקְלִיפִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It stays on the general theme of מוקצה but is a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: bones and shells may be cleared directly. בית הלל: one lifts the tabletop and shakes them off.

steps.title: משנה: Crumbs and pods may be cleared because animals eat them
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that one may clear crumbs smaller than a כזית, and pea and lentil pods, because these are animal food.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may clear from the table crumbs smaller than a כזית, and pea pods and lentil pods, because it is animal food.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second ruling about clearing the table. Here it allows moving certain small leftovers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tiny crumbs and pods are not normal human food, so you might think they are worthless and therefore מוקצה. The משנה says they may still be moved, because they are fit for animals. Being animal food counts as a use, so they are not set aside.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than the size of an olive

steps.whatToRemember: Something that is still useful as animal food may be moved, even if people would not eat it. Step 10 shows that this ruling follows רבי שמעון, who does not hold of מוקצה.

phrases.english: One may clear from the table
crumbs less than an olive-bulk,
and pea pods
and lentil pods,
because it is animal fodder.
phrases.notes: This explains why these items are not מוקצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲבִירִין מִלִּפְנֵי הַשֻּׁלְחָן פֵּירוּרִין פָּחוֹת מִכְּזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a second ruling, about crumbs and pods.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Crumbs smaller than a כזית and pea and lentil pods may be cleared from the table, because they are animal food.

steps.title: Wiping the table with a sponge on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends with a dispute about a sponge. The first opinion says it may be used only if it has a leather handle. The חכמים say it may be moved either way and it cannot become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a sponge has a leather handle, you may wipe the table with it. If it does not, you may not wipe with it. The חכמים say: either way it may be moved on שבת, and it does not become טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of table-clearing rules with a case about wiping the table with a sponge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sponge soaks up liquid, so holding it directly may squeeze liquid out, which is forbidden on שבת (סחיטה). A leather handle lets you hold it without squeezing, so the first opinion permits wiping only then. The חכמים permit moving the sponge in both cases and add that it is not something that can become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A handle, a place to grip

phrases.aramaic: סְפוֹג, אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ עוֹר בֵּית אֲחִיזָה
phrases.english: A sponge: if it has leather as a handle
phrases.notes: The handle lets you hold it without squeezing the sponge itself.

phrases.english: one may wipe with it,
and if not, one may not wipe with it.
phrases.notes: The worry is that he will squeeze liquid out.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ נִיטָּל בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: either way, it may be moved on Shabbat,
and it does not become ritually impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְפוֹג, אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ עוֹר בֵּית אֲחִיזָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה about clearing the table on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First opinion: one may wipe with a sponge only if it has a leather handle. חכמים: it may be moved either way and does not become טמא.

steps.title: רב נחמן reverses בית שמאי and בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says his tradition is the reverse of our משנה. בית שמאי follow the strict view of רבי יהודה on מוקצה, and בית הלל follow the lenient view of רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Our tradition is only that בית שמאי hold like רבי יהודה, and בית הלל hold like רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רב נחמן says that the opinions of בית שמאי and בית הלל in the bones-and-shells dispute (step 4) should be switched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, בית שמאי allow removing bones directly, which is lenient like רבי שמעון. בית הלל require shaking off the tabletop, which is strict like רבי יהודה. רב נחמן says to flip them: בית הלל are the ones who allow removing bones and shells directly, because they hold there is no מוקצה here.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
We have (as our tradition) only this
Items set aside, which may not be moved on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the sides. In the משנה as printed, בית הלל are strict. According to רב נחמן, בית הלל are the lenient ones, like רבי שמעון, and the הלכה follows בית הלל.
steps.whyThisMatters: Since the הלכה follows בית הלל, this reversal means that in practice one may clear bones and shells directly from the table.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Nachman said:
We have only this (as our tradition):
Beit Shammai hold like Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה forbids moving מוקצה.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel hold like Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון permits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אָנוּ אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first comment of the גמרא on the משנה. It goes back to the bones-and-shells dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reverse the opinions: בית שמאי follow רבי יהודה (strict) and בית הלל follow רבי שמעון (lenient).

steps.title: The crumbs ruling supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's rule about clearing crumbs supports רבי יוחנן, who says it is forbidden to destroy crumbs smaller than a כזית with one's hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one may clear crumbs from the table. This supports רבי יוחנן, who said: crumbs smaller than a כזית may not be destroyed by hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling about crumbs and points out that it supports a statement of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה found it necessary to say that crumbs smaller than a כזית may be cleared (מעבירין) from the table. That shows even such small crumbs are still treated as significant food and are carefully removed, not thrown away. This fits רבי יוחנן's rule that, out of respect for food, you may not destroy small crumbs with your hands.

keyTerms.meaning: To destroy them with one's hands

phrases.english: (The משנה said:) One may clear crumbs from the table.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה (step 5).

phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Yochanan,
for Rabbi Yochanan said:
crumbs that are less than an olive-size
it is forbidden to destroy them by hand.
phrases.notes: Out of respect for food.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate comment on the משנה, about the crumbs.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that crumbs smaller than a כזית may not be destroyed by hand.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that crumbs smaller than a כזית are cleared (removed) from the table, which shows they are significant food.

steps.title: Whose view is the pods ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling about pea pods and asks which תנא it follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: pea pods may be cleared. Whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the pods ruling and asks whose opinion it is. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pods are only animal food. Nobody set them aside for animals before שבת, so it is not obvious that they may be moved. The גמרא wants to know which view of מוקצה allows this.

phrases.english: (The משנה said:) pea pods (may be cleared).
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה (step 5).

phrases.english: Whose opinion is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: שֵׂעָר שֶׁל אֲפוּנִין. מַנִּי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, separate comment on the משנה, about the pods.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view of מוקצה allows moving pea pods on שבת.

steps.title: The pods ruling follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The pods ruling follows רבי שמעון, who does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי שמעון, who does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the ruling about pods follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, pods that were not set aside for animals before שבת would be מוקצה and could not be moved. רבי שמעון does not hold of this kind of מוקצה, so for him the pods may be moved and cleared away. This fits רב נחמן's point that בית הלל and the הלכה follow רבי שמעון here.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who is lenient about מוקצה

steps.whatToRemember: Three notes on the משנה: (1) רב נחמן reverses the opinions, so בית הלל are lenient like רבי שמעון. (2) The crumbs ruling supports רבי יוחנן: small crumbs may not be destroyed by hand. (3) The pods ruling follows רבי שמעון, who does not hold of מוקצה.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Shimon,
who does not hold of set-aside (muktzeh).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא, דְּלֵית לֵיהּ מוּקְצֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The pods ruling follows רבי שמעון, who does not hold of מוקצה.

steps.title: The sponge ruling seems to follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה, about the sponge, seems to follow רבי יהודה. But the pods ruling just before it followed רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the end of the משנה: a sponge with a handle may be used for wiping, and without one it may not. That sounds like רבי יהודה, who forbids a דבר שאין מתכוין, an act done without intending the forbidden result.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If the משנה follows רבי שמעון, why does its last case sound like רבי יהודה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a handle, wiping with a sponge squeezes out liquid. The person does not want to squeeze, so this is a דבר שאין מתכוין. רבי שמעון permits such acts and רבי יהודה forbids them, so forbidding the sponge looks like רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a משנה
A handle, a place to hold it
An act done without intending the forbidden result
'We have arrived at', meaning this matches the view of...

steps.confusionAlert: The issue here is not מוקצה. It is squeezing liquid from the sponge (סחיטה), which the person does not intend.

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:

phrases.aramaic: סְפוֹג, אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ בֵּית אֲחִיזָה —
phrases.english: A sponge, if it has a handle —
one may wipe with it,
and if not, one may not wipe with it.
We have arrived at Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: This seems to switch to the opposing view.

phrases.english: who said: an unintended act is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 10's claim that the משנה follows רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה follows רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sponge ruling forbids an unintended act, which is רבי יהודה's view. So the משנה would be split between two תנאים.

steps.title: Even רבי שמעון forbids an act whose result is certain
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון agrees in a case of פסיק רישיה, and squeezing a sponge is exactly that kind of case.
steps.simpleTranslation: In this case even רבי שמעון agrees it is forbidden. אביי and רבא both said that רבי שמעון agrees when the result is as certain as 'cut off its head, and will it not die?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the sponge ruling fits רבי שמעון too. So the whole משנה can follow רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון permits unintended acts only when the forbidden result might not happen. Wiping with a sponge that has no handle will certainly squeeze out liquid, so it counts as a פסיק רישיה. In that kind of case רבי שמעון also forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Cut off its head and will it not die?': a forbidden result that is certain to happen

steps.whyThisMatters: פסיק רישיה is a basic principle of הלכות שבת. An unintended act is permitted only if the forbidden result is not certain.

phrases.english: In this case, even Rabbi Shimon agrees,
for Abaye and Rava both say:
Rabbi Shimon agrees
in a case of 'cut off its head, and will it not die?'
phrases.notes: The forbidden result is unavoidable.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהָא אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מוֹדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the case is one where the other opinion also agrees
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sponge ruling must follow רבי יהודה, since it forbids an unintended act.
steps.terutzMaskana: Squeezing the sponge is a פסיק רישיה, which רבי שמעון also forbids. So the whole משנה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון permits a דבר שאין מתכוין, except when it is a פסיק רישיה.

steps.title: Pits of Aramean dates may be moved, but pits of Persian dates may not
steps.stepSummary: Pits of cheap Aramean dates may be moved on שבת, because the dates themselves were fit for animals. Pits of Persian dates may not be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: The pits of Aramean dates may be moved, since they are fit for use along with their 'mother', the date. Moving the pits of Persian dates is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a new ruling about leftovers on שבת. It is about moving date pits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Aramean dates are low quality and are sometimes given to animals. Since the fruit was ready for animal use before שבת, its pits share that status and are not מוקצה. Persian dates are fine fruit that are not given to animals, so their pits have no prepared use and are forbidden to move.

keyTerms.meaning: By virtue of their 'mother', the fruit they came from

phrases.english: These pits of Aramean dates,
it is permitted to move them,
since they are fit for use by virtue of their mother (the date).
But those of Persian dates are forbidden to move.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי גַּרְעִינִין דְּתַמְרֵי אֲרַמָּיָיתָא שְׁרוּ לְטַלְטוֹלִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling on the same theme of leftovers and מוקצה on שבת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pit gets the status of its fruit. If the fruit was fit for animals, its pit may be moved. If not, the pit is מוקצה.

steps.title: שמואל carried pits on top of bread
steps.stepSummary: שמואל would move forbidden pits by carrying them along with bread. A memory aid lists the names in the coming statements.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל would move the pits by carrying them along with bread. The letters שרנ״ם שפ״ז are a memory aid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports what שמואל did in practice. It then gives a memory aid for the sages quoted in the next part of the sugya.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל put the pits on a piece of bread and carried the bread. The bread is permitted to move, and the pits came along with it. The memory aid stands for שמואל, רבה, הונא, אמימר, ששת, פפא, זכריה.
steps.confusionAlert: שרנ״ם שפ״ז is not a word or a ruling. It is only a memory aid listing names.

phrases.english: Shmuel would move them along with bread.
(Shin-Resh-Nun-Mem, Shin-Peh-Zayin is a mnemonic.)
phrases.notes: The letters stand for: שמואל, רבה, הונא, אמימר, ששת, פפא, זכריה.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל מְטַלְטֵל לְהוּ אַגַּב רִיפְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a practical way to move pits that may not be moved directly
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forbidden pits may be moved by carrying them on bread, which is permitted to move.

steps.title: שמואל follows his rule that bread may be used for any need
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's practice fits his own principle that a person may use bread for all his needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל is following his own reasoning, for שמואל said: a person may do all his needs with bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שמואל was comfortable using bread to carry pits. He holds that using bread this way is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think that using bread as a tray for pits treats food with disrespect. שמואל holds that as long as the bread stays edible, it may be used for any purpose. So his practice matches his own known ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning, consistent with his own view

steps.whatToRemember: Date pits follow their fruit's status. שמואל carried pits on bread, because he holds bread may be used for any need as long as it stays edible.

phrases.english: Shmuel follows his own reasoning,
for Shmuel said:
A person may do all his needs with bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind שמואל's practice in step 14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bread may be used for one's needs, such as carrying things on it, as long as it remains edible.

steps.title: רבה carried the pits along with a water pitcher
steps.stepSummary: רבה moved the forbidden pits by carrying them together with a permitted pitcher of water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה would move them (the pits) along with a pitcher of water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the list of אמוראים and how each one handled date pits on שבת. רבה moved the pits together with a water pitcher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like שמואל's practice with bread. The pitcher is a permitted object, and the pits are carried 'along with' it. Moving something permitted can bring along the מוקצה item with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Along with; by means of something else

phrases.english: Rabba would move them
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the forbidden date pits from the previous steps.

phrases.english: along with a pitcher of water.
phrases.notes: The pitcher is permitted, so the pits are carried together with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה מְטַלְטֵל לְהוּ אַגַּב לָקָנָא דְמַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another אמורא's practice to the list begun with שמואל and the bread.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forbidden pits may be moved together with a permitted object like a water pitcher.

steps.title: רב הונא treated the pits like a chamber pot
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע gathered the pits so they became disgusting, like a גרף של רעי, which may be removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע would make them like a chamber pot with excrement.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא's method. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע treated the pile of pits like a גרף של רעי, a disgusting container that חכמים allow you to take out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים permitted removing a repulsive object, like a chamber pot, even on שבת, because nobody should have to live with it. רב הונא collected the pits until the pile was disgusting, and then he removed it under that same permission.

keyTerms.meaning: A chamber pot with excrement; a repulsive object that may be removed on שבת
He made them into, he treated them as

phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua,
would make them like a chamber pot with excrement.
phrases.notes: He gathered the pits until they were disgusting, then removed them as one removes a chamber pot.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עָבֵיד לְהוּ כִּגְרָף שֶׁל רֶיעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another practice in the same list, but it uses a different legal tool: the permission to remove repulsive things.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pits are removed under the permission given for a גרף של רעי.

steps.title: רב אשי asks: may one create a chamber pot on purpose?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges רב הונא's method: the permission covers an existing גרף של רעי, not one made on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: But may one make a chamber pot with excrement in the first place?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges this chamber-pot method, addressing אמימר, who evidently acted the same way as רב הונא (אמימר is the מ in the memory aid). He says you may remove a disgusting thing that is already there, but you may not create one on purpose just to make it movable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission for a גרף של רעי exists because the mess happened, not because you planned it. רב הונא created the disgusting pile himself, so the permission should not apply. The גמרא gives no answer, so the challenge stands.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, deliberately, ahead of time
But is it really so that...? Opens a challenging question

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי does not deny that a גרף של רעי may be removed. He only objects to creating one on purpose (לכתחילה) so that the permission will apply.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי עוֹשִׂין גְּרָף שֶׁל רֶיעִי לְכַתְּחִילָּה?
phrases.english: And may one create a chamber pot with excrement in the first place?
phrases.notes: A question that works as a challenge: you may remove one, but you may not make one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי עוֹשִׂין גְּרָף שֶׁל רֶיעִי לְכַתְּחִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges the method described in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of treating the pits as a גרף של רעי, done by רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע and, by implication, by אמימר, to whom the challenge is addressed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The permission to remove a repulsive object only covers one that already exists. Creating one on purpose to use the permission is not allowed.

steps.title: רב ששת removed the pits with his tongue
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת never took the pits in his hand. He pushed them out of his mouth with his tongue.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת would throw them out with his tongue.
steps.whatsHappening: The list goes on with another method. רב ששת got rid of the pits straight from his mouth using his tongue, so he never handled them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he never picked up the pits with his hand, he never moved מוקצה in the usual way. This avoids the problem completely.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet would dispose of them with his tongue.
phrases.notes: He spat them out without touching them by hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת זָרֵיק לְהוּ בְּלִישָּׁנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge to רב הונא, the list moves to a method that has no such problem.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Removing pits directly from the mouth with the tongue avoids handling מוקצה.

steps.title: רב פפא tossed the pits behind the couch
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא threw the pits behind the couch he sat on while eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא would throw them behind the couch.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא's method. רב פפא threw the pits right away behind the couch where he was eating, so he would not need to move them later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the pits are out of the way behind the couch, there is no need to carry them anywhere. He gets rid of them at once instead of moving them around afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: Behind the couch (the couch people reclined on while eating)

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא זָרֵיק לְהוּ אֲחוֹרֵי הַמִּטָּה.
phrases.english: Rav Pappa would dispose of them behind the couch.
phrases.notes: Thrown right away, out of the way, so they would not need moving later.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא זָרֵיק לְהוּ אֲחוֹרֵי הַמִּטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another practice in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pits may be tossed right away behind the couch so they never need to be moved.

steps.title: רבי זכריה בן אבקולס did the same
steps.stepSummary: A report about רבי זכריה בן אבקולס, who turned toward the back of the couch and threw the pits there. This matches רב פפא's practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבי זכריה בן אבקולס that he would turn his face toward the back of the couch and throw them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an earlier story that matches רב פפא's practice. רבי זכריה בן אבקולס also threw the pits behind the couch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זכריה בן אבקולס was known for being very careful in his conduct. If he used this method, it shows that throwing pits behind the couch is a proper way to act. He even turned his face so the pits would land out of the way.

keyTerms.meaning: They said about him (introduces a report about a person's conduct)

steps.whatToRemember: Each אמורא found his own way to get rid of מוקצה pits: carrying them along with something permitted (bread, a water pitcher), removing them with the tongue, or tossing them aside right away. Creating a disgusting object on purpose (רב הונא's method) was challenged.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי זְכַרְיָה בֶּן אַבְקוּלָס
phrases.english: They said about Rabbi Zekharya ben Avkolas
phrases.notes: This is a story about how an earlier sage behaved himself.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה מַחֲזִיר פָּנָיו אֲחוֹרֵי הַמִּטָּה וְזוֹרְקָן.
phrases.english: that he would turn his face toward the back of the couch and dispose of them.
phrases.notes: Same method as רב פפא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי זְכַרְיָה בֶּן אַבְקוּלָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב פפא's practice with an earlier precedent.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's practice of throwing pits behind the couch
steps.raayaSupportSource: The report about the conduct of רבי זכריה בן אבקולס

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter נוטל אדם את בנו
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the פרק נוטל אדם את בנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, נוטל אדם את בנו.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. It is the traditional closing line said at the end of a פרק, and this one ends פרק נוטל אדם את בנו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן formula expresses the wish to return and learn this פרק again. It marks the end of this chapter's discussions about מוקצה and moving things on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (closing formula for a chapter)
'A person may take his son' — the name of this פרק, taken from its opening words

phrases.aramaic: הדרן עלך נוטל אדם את בנו
phrases.english: We will return to you, 'A person may take his son'
phrases.notes: This is the traditional line said when finishing a פרק.

steps.triggerLanguage: הדרן עלך נוטל אדם את בנו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the chapter after the last practice is reported.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of פרק נוטל אדם את בנו.
